Name of the surah

• It is called Al-Hijr, because it mentions the people of Salih (peace be upon him), namely the tribe of Thamud, who used to dwell in al-Hijr, which is the present-day ruins of Salih's cities (Madain Salih). They were named after their place of residence.

From the objectives of the surah

• Extolling the virtue of the Qur'an and its guidance, warning the polytheists of a regret they will feel for not embracing Islam, rebuking them for being preoccupied with desires instead of guidance, and warning them of destruction when punishment arrives.

• Establishing proof against the disbelievers through the magnificent handiwork of God in the cosmic signs in the heavens and the earth, as evidence of God's power to give life, cause death, resurrect and recompense; consoling the Messenger (ﷺ) for their lack of faith and for what they say about him; and explaining that this is the custom of the deniers with their messengers, and that their denial is out of obstinacy, not out of any deficiency in the evidences of faith.

• Mention of the human species and the honour God bestowed upon it, explanation of the origin of guidance and misguidance, the fate of the misguided and the guided, the mention of the story of Satan's disbelief and his oath to mislead all the people of the earth, except those whom God has chosen for guidance and success.

• Mention of some of the stories of earlier prophets with their peoples, and explanation of what befell those who opposed them; as consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ) and as strengthening for him until certainty comes to him; and an indication of the reward of those who obey and the punishment of those who oppose the call of the Prophet (ﷺ); his (ﷺ) being commanded to pardon those who harm him, and being informed that God is sufficient for him against his enemies.

In this there is a warning and a deterrent to them against persisting in these ugly deeds.
So proclaim openly the call to the truth that Allah has commanded you to convey, and do not concern yourself with the polytheists, for Allah has cleared you of what they say.

Indeed, We have sufficed you against the mockers, the scoffing leaders of Quraysh, who took partners with Allah from among the idols and others. So they will soon come to know the consequence of their deeds, in this world and in the Hereafter.

We know, O Messenger, that your chest is constricted because of what the polytheists say about you and your call.

So flee to your Lord when your chest is constricted, glorify Him with His praise, thanking Him and extolling Him, and be among those who pray and worship Him. For that will suffice you against what distresses you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 15, verse 99:

Continue in the worship of your Lord for as long as you live, until there comes to you the certainty (al-yaqin), which is death. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) complied with the command of his Lord, and he never ceased being diligent in the worship of Allah, until there came to him the certainty from his Lord.
